questions.question: Identify the part of the following sentence that contains an error in subject–verb agreement. The panel of climate scientists, together with several policy advisors and environmental activists, is preparing a comprehensive report, but neither the findings from the recent studies nor the recommendations issued by international organizations appear to reflect the urgency of the situation, which, despite widespread awareness, continue to be overlooked by many governments that prioritize economic gains over environmental sustainability.
questions.questionHtml:

options.html: The panel of climate scientists, together with several policy advisors and environmental activists, is preparing a comprehensive report

options.text: but neither the findings from the recent studies nor the recommendations issued by international organizations appear to reflect the urgency of the situation
options.html: but neither the findings from the recent studies nor the recommendations issued by international organizations appear to reflect the urgency of the situation

options.text: which, despite widespread awareness, continue to be overlooked by many governments
options.html: which, despite widespread awareness, continue to be overlooked by many governments

options.html: that prioritize economic gains over environmental sustainability

questions.solution:
The incorrect subject-verb agreement in the sentence is:

“…which, despite widespread awareness, continue to be overlooked…”

Error: The relative pronoun “which” refers to the entire situation, a singular noun. So, the verb should be “continues”, not “continue”.

Corrected version: “…which, despite widespread awareness, continues to be overlooked by many governments…

questions.question: Read the passage carefully and answer the following questions. On October 19, 2025, one of the most audacious crimes in art history took place at the Louvre Museum in Paris. In just seven minutes, an organized gang executed a daylight heist, fleeing with priceless jewels and artifacts. The robbers arrived in a truck disguised as construction workers, using a crane to access a high window in the Apollo Gallery. They wore reflective clothing to blend in with their surroundings, and used angle grinders to break glass display cases. Inside, they seized rare royal jewels, including crowns and diadems, which represented centuries of history and craftsmanship. The robbers swiftly escaped on motorcycles, leaving behind one damaged crown of Empress Eugenie. The security system was outdated, with only one camera monitoring the scene, which the museum admitted was inadequate. Authorities are investigating, but the theft has severely impacted France's cultural heritage, sparking outrage worldwide. The stolen items, symbols of monarchial power and artistry, remain missing, and the event has become a wakeup call for global museums to upgrade their security systems. Experts say that this heist was meticulously planned, with the robbers demonstrating military precision. The incident weakened public confidence in the security of even the most protected institutions. The Louvre, an icon of art and history, was temporarily closed for security re-evaluation. This daring theft not only caused economic loss but also portrayed the vulnerability of cultural treasures in a modern world of rising art crimes. What is the main idea of the passage about the Louvre Museum heist?

questions.solution: The passage mentions that during the heist, thieves stole nine items of priceless jewellery, including crown jewels, diadems, necklaces, and brooches belonging to French royalty such as Empress Eugenie and Napoleonic period artifacts. There is no mention of paintings, manuscripts, or weapons being stolen in this incident.
